html:
The journey of the Bengali Buddhist master Atisha from the monastery of Vikramashila in India to Tibet. He set out in 1040 and reached the western Tibetan kingdom of Guge in 1042.

After the Tibetan Empire collapsed in the 840s, organised Buddhism in central Tibet had largely broken down. The kings of Guge set out to restore it with teachers from India. After years of invitations and gifts of gold, Atisha, then about sixty and one of the most respected scholars of the Pala lands, agreed to go. He crossed through Nepal and over the Himalaya.

He meant to stay a few years but never went back. He taught in Guge and then in central Tibet until his death in 1054. He reformed monastic discipline and set out a clear, step-by-step path in his Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment. His Tibetan disciple Dromtonpa founded the Kadam school, whose teachings were later absorbed by the Gelug school, the school of the Dalai Lamas. The same journey is told from the Tibetan side in Atisha comes to Tibet.
sum: The journey of the Bengali Buddhist master Atisha from the monastery of Vikramashila in India to Tibet. He set out in 1040 and reached the western Tibetan kingdom of Guge in 1042.
